title: Cleanup must not delete artifacts from an actively served workspace
summary: A cleanup helper can break a preview or verification endpoint when it deletes build artifacts from the same workspace that a process, mount, or proxy is still serving.
ai_value: Helps agents distinguish disposable worktrees from active serving directories before closeout cleanup, and prevents false confidence from root-HTML-only smoke checks.

contexts: cleanup, closeout, or worklane-finish automation is about to delete generated assets, caches, dependencies, or a worktree
the same path may be used by a local preview, verification server, container mount, service manager, or reverse proxy
static assets, hydration, or authentication UI matter to the next operator

trigger_signals.description: A workspace is both a development desk and the current serving directory for a preview or verification endpoint.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Treat the filesystem path as runtime state, not disposable residue.
trigger_signals.pattern: serving directory|preview endpoint|verification server|current working directory|bind mount

trigger_signals.description: A generic finish wrapper designed for throwaway worktrees is being used on a standing lane, shared desk, or long-lived checkout.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Reclassify the workspace before deleting build output or caches.

trigger_signals.description: After cleanup, root HTML still loads but static assets, hydration, or auth UI fail.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Smoke asset URLs and primary UI flows, not only the root route.

negative_signals.description: The target is a genuinely disposable non-serving worktree with no active process, mount, or service dependency.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Removing the whole disposable tree is not this trap when no runtime depends on the path.

negative_signals.description: The serving target has already been switched away and the replacement was rebuilt and smoked.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Cleanup after traffic/process handoff is a different, safer state.

common_wrong_assumptions: Completed work does not imply its workspace is disposable.
If the root HTML loads, the preview is healthy.
A cleanup wrapper is safe everywhere because it was safe for throwaway worktrees.

first_checks.check: Classify the workspace as throwaway, standing, shared default checkout, or active serving directory before deletion.
first_checks.why: The cleanup safety boundary depends on workspace role, not task completion state.

first_checks.check: Check processes, service configs, container mounts, and proxy metadata for references to the target path.
first_checks.why: Runtime references turn filesystem cleanup into availability-impacting cleanup.

first_checks.check: Smoke static asset URLs and the primary authenticated or hydrated UI path after any reset.
first_checks.why: Root HTML can pass while the actual app is broken.

decision_rules.condition: A cleanup target is still referenced by a running process, mount, service config, or proxy.
decision_rules.then: Do not delete build artifacts; switch or stop the dependent runtime through the approved path, then rebuild and smoke before reporting cleanup complete.

decision_rules.condition: No active runtime references the disposable worktree and no shared lane uses it.
decision_rules.then: Proceed with normal cleanup and record the classification evidence.

do_not: Do not delete build output, dependency directories, or framework caches from a long-lived serving workspace as routine closeout.
Do not release a lease and infer that filesystem artifacts can be removed.
Do not verify only the root HTML page after cleanup.

Do not include private service names, internal URLs, account identifiers, incident identifiers, private repository paths, tenant/store names, setup-card field names, low-level endpoint strings or organization-specific tooling in public lessons.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Classify the path, prove no runtime depends on it, and smoke assets plus the primary UI before deleting generated artifacts.

risk.notes: This public record is de-identified and does not authorize live mutation, publication, credential, permission, billing, data, or availability changes by itself.
